# xpile_wasm_codegen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-wasm-codegen/^0.1.12/

## Expand description

Native WebAssembly backend — the EMIT half of first-class bidirectional native WASM (PMAT-951).

Lowers the meta-HIR **scalar/control subset** directly to
WebAssembly Text format (WAT) text, emitted into [ Artifact::primary](https://docs.rs/xpile-backend/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_backend/struct.Artifact.html#structfield.primary)
as a

`String` — **no runtime dependency**(a String-emitter shape, the same posture as the PTX/WGSL scaffold emitters, but here a

*real*meta-HIR lowering rather than a hardcoded shader).

This is the tractable (high→low) direction of the bidirectional WASM
goal: structured meta-HIR (funcs/locals/if/loops/i64/f64/calls) →
WASM. It deliberately does NOT go through the Ruchy `WasmEmitter` hop
(the spec §73/§484 delegated-only stance, now superseded) — xpile owns
the lane, exactly as the cuda-oxide “own it, drop the delegation”
decision (`project-gpu-cuda-oxide-wgpu-first-class`).

[§](https://docs.rs#supported-subset)Supported subset

- Types: `I64`/`CLong`→`i64`,`F64`→`f64`,`F32`→`f32`,`Bool`→`i32`(WASM has no bool; 0/1 in an i32), and a 32-bit-ish`CUInt`→`i32`. Everything else (`Dict`/`Set`/`Struct`/`Tuple`/`BigInt`/`Optional`/pointers/…) is**refused**with`BackendError::Lower`
- The FIRST string support (PMAT-986 slice 1): a `str`**parameter**lowers to an`i32`base-pointer into WASM**linear memory**, mirroring the`list[scalar]`ABI exactly — an`i32`UTF-8**byte count**at`base+0`, then the raw UTF-8 bytes from`base+8`(the same 8-byte header offset the list layout uses). As of**PMAT-1032**every Python-VISIBLE string read is**CHAR-oriented (code points)**over that byte-oriented ABI — sweep #11 (PMAT-1031 finding 2) confirmed the old byte-oriented reads SILENTLY diverged on non-ASCII input: (1)`len(s)``$__wasm_str_charlen`(a non-continuation-byte count —`len("héllo")`is 5, matching CPython, where the header holds 6 bytes); and (2)`ord(s[i])``Expr::Ord`over an`Expr::StrCharAt`of a str name) lowers to`$__wasm_str_ord_at`— a CHAR-indexed walk + 1..4-byte UTF-8 decode, with Python NEGATIVE-index normalisation (`s[-1]`reads from the end) and the bounds trap (`unreachable`, the`IndexError`analogue) inside the helper.`ord(ch)`over a 1-char str name guards`charlen != 1 → unreachable`(the`TypeError`analogue) — the CHAR count, so`ord("é")`decodes to 233 exactly. As of**PMAT-993 (slice 2)**string-RETURNING ops are unblocked by a linear-memory**bump allocator**(`(global $__heap_ptr (mut i32))`past the static`(data)`region plus`$__alloc(n)`, 8-byte-aligned, bump-only with no free; see`HEAP_BASE`/`heap_helpers`). The slice-2 string ops:**string concatenation**(`a + b``Expr::Concat`) does`alloc(8 + Σ len(opᵢ))`, writes the count header,`memory.copy`s each operand’s bytes, and returns the new base-pointer (left-nested`(a+b)+c`flattens to ONE alloc with N copies) — concat/copy/equality stay BYTE ops (byte equality IS char equality for UTF-8); and`chr(n)``Expr::Chr`) lowers to`$__wasm_chr`— the full 1..4-byte UTF-8 encoding of code point`n`, trapping outside`0..=0x10FFFF`(the`ValueError`analogue; the pre-PMAT-1032 lowering masked`n & 0xFF`, silently wrong for n > 127). A function RETURNING a`str`works (the result is the new string’s`i32`heap pointer). As of**PMAT-994 (slice 3a)**string support is substantially complete: (1) string**LITERALS**(`Expr::LitStr`, e.g.`"Hello, "`) are materialised at emit time into static`(data …)`segments in`[LITERAL_BASE, HEAP_BASE)`(length-prefixed, the same ABI), and a`LitStr`lowers to a constant`i32.const <base>`— so`"Hi " + name`,`return "done"`, and literal args all work; (2)`s[i]`as a 1-char string`Expr::StrCharAt`outside`ord`) materialises a new 1-char heap string via`$__wasm_str_char_at`(the full encoded char, 1..4 bytes, char-indexed + negative-index-normalised since PMAT-1032); and (3) string**content equality**`a == b`/`a != b`lowers to a`$__wasm_str_eq`helper (length check + byte-compare loop → i32 bool) — REAL content logic, never a base-pointer compare. Since PMAT-1058/1059 string**slicing**`s[lo:hi]`and**ordering**(`<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=`) are supported, and since PMAT-1060`str(int)`/`repr(int)``Expr::ToStr { of_float: false }`) materialises an i64’s decimal-ASCII form via`$__wasm_int_to_str`(unsigned-magnitude, so`i64::MIN`is exact). Still**refused**honestly (a hard`BackendError`):`str(float)`/`repr(float)`, f-strings, string methods, and the composite`dict`/`set`value/`in`shapes not yet wired. Char access is O(chars) per read (charlen is O(bytes)) — correctness over speed, an honest documented tradeoff.
- The FIRST aggregate (PMAT-966 + PMAT-968): a `list[int]`/`list[float]`**parameter**lowers to an`i32`base-pointer into WASM**linear memory**. As of PMAT-968 the pointed-at region is a length-prefixed layout: an`i32`element**count**at`base+0`, then the packed elements starting at`base+8`(the 8-byte offset keeps every`i64`/`f64`element naturally aligned). This length header unlocks two PMAT-968 deliverables that PMAT-966 deliberately refused — (1)**bounds-checked**, where the`xs[i]``Index`lowering loads the header length and emits a guard`i < 0 || i >= len → unreachable`(a WASM trap) BEFORE the`*.load`, the faithful Python`IndexError`analogue (PMAT-966 let an out-of-range address silently mis-read or trap only on an unmapped page); and (2)`len(xs)``Expr::Len`), lowered to an`i32.load`of the header count zero-extended to the`i64`Python-int domain. The element type must itself be a supported scalar (`i64`/`f64`/`f32`); a`list[bool]`, nested list, or list of strings is refused. As of PMAT-978 a single-index**write**`xs[i] = v`(`Stmt::IndexAssign`) is also supported — the mutation companion of the read path, reusing the SAME bounds guard + address math but terminating in a natural-width`*.store`. As of**PMAT-1033**a`list[scalar]`**LOCAL**(`xs: list[int] = [1, 2, 3]`) binds too: the`ListLit`materialises a fresh length-prefixed record on the bump heap (the same ABI a param rides, so`xs[i]`/`xs[i] = v`/`len(xs)`and the PMAT-1030`for x in xs`desugar work over it verbatim), and a list-name binding (`ys = xs`) is a bare pointer copy — Python’s aliasing, native to linear memory. A list**return**, list**append**/ growth (fixed-size records; growth would relocate and break aliases — the PMAT-999 posture), list-returning calls, and a MULTI-index / nested-list write (`xs[i][j] = v`) remain refused.
- Statements: `Let`/`Assign`(→`local`+`local.set`),`If`/`While`/`Break`/`Continue`/`Return`,`xs[i] = v`(`IndexAssign`) over a`list[scalar]`param (bounds-checked`*.store`), and as of**PMAT-1023**`obj.field = v`(`FieldAssign`— a`*.store`at the field’s 8-byte-slot offset) plus statement-position method calls (`SideEffectCall`over an`Expr::MethodCall`, dropping a discarded result) and, as of PMAT-1024, statement-position PLAIN function calls (`SideEffectCall`over an`Expr::Call`— the`bump(c)`mutating-helper idiom the reference-aware frontend passes through as a bare heap pointer).
- Expressions: `Ident`(→`local.get`),`LitInt`/`LitFloat`/`LitBool`,`BinOp`(arith/bitwise/shift + comparisons),`FloatBinOp`,`UnOp`,`IfExpr`,`Index`over a`list[scalar]`param (bounds-checked`*.load`),`Len`over a`list[scalar]`param (→ header`i32.load`+`i64`extend), a direct intra-module`Call`, and`obj.method(args)`(`MethodCall`) over a struct local/param receiver.
- **Struct METHODS (PMAT-1023):**each- `Item::Struct`method — including SELF-MUTATING ones (- `self.count = self.count + 1`) — emits as an ordinary WAT function- `$<Struct>.<method>`whose- `self`receiver is the instance’s- `i32`base-pointer. A field write through- `self`(or any struct local/param) is a store through that pointer, so the mutation is visible to EVERY binding of the record: Python’s reference semantics are NATIVE to linear memory — no clone/refuse alias disposition needed (the Rust lane must refuse shapes this lane executes exactly). Struct- `==`/ordering is REFUSED honestly (a struct rides an i32 base-pointer; a naive compare would be pointer identity, not Python’s structural- `==`), as are non-- `self`receivers and unknown methods.

[§](https://docs.rs#semantic-posture-replicated-from-the-rustptx-lanes)Semantic posture (replicated from the Rust/PTX lanes)

- `C-PY-INT-ARITH`overflow:- `i64.add`/- `sub`/- `mul`WRAP silently in WASM (two’s-complement modular). The Python contract bounds overflow, so for- `I64`arithmetic the emitter inserts an explicit checked sequence that- **traps**(- `unreachable`) on signed overflow rather than silently wrapping — matching the Rust lane’s checked-arithmetic panic posture. (- `CUInt`modular wrapping is the- *defined*C semantics, so it uses bare- `i32`ops.)
- **FloorDiv / Mod:**WASM- `i64.div_s`truncates toward zero and traps on divide-by-zero;- `i64.rem_s`is the truncating remainder. Python’s- `//`/- `%`floor toward −∞ and the remainder takes the divisor’s sign, so the emitter applies the same floor correction the Rust lane uses (- `div_euclid`/- `rem_euclid`-equivalent), implemented inline in WAT.

Layer 5 compile contract: `contracts/compile-rust-to-wasm-v1.yaml`
(`C-COMPILE-RUST-TO-WASM`), proof lane `contracts/lean/XlateRustToWasm.lean`.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Wasm](https://docs.rs/struct.WasmBackend.html)- Backend
- Native WASM backend. Lowers the meta-HIR scalar/control subset to WAT
text. `Backend`impl (single-emitter — no §29 quorum at this slice; the executed two-emitter`WasmDiffExecEngine`witness is deferred to PMAT-952).
- [Wasm](https://docs.rs/struct.WasmDiffExecEngine.html)- Diff - Exec - Engine
- A real WASM `DiffExecEngine`: assembles each emitter’s WAT module with`wat2wasm`, executes both with`wasm-interp --run-all-exports`, and numerically compares the outputs. This is the executed Run≥1 witness for`C-COMPILE-RUST-TO-WASM`.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [FIXTURE_](https://docs.rs/constant.FIXTURE_INPUT.html)- INPUT
- The deterministic fixture input vector both WAT modules run over. Kept
**bit-identical**to [`xpile_ptx_codegen::FIXTURE_INPUT`] / [`xpile_wgsl_codegen::FIXTURE_INPUT`] so the WASM, CUDA, and WGSL executed witnesses attest the same values on different stacks; exercises negatives, zero, a fraction, and a larger magnitude.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [emit_](https://docs.rs/fn.emit_module.html)- module
- Emit a full `(module …)`for`module`. Only`Item::Function`
- [general_](https://docs.rs/fn.general_module_wat.html)- module_ - wat
- PMAT-976: emit REAL xpile WAT for the general side via `emit_module`
- [wasm_](https://docs.rs/fn.wasm_runtime_available.html)- runtime_ - available
- `true`when both- `wat2wasm`and- `wasm-interp`(WABT) are invocable — the gate that decides whether- `WasmDiffExecEngine`- `xpile_ptx_codegen::cuda_toolchain_available`] / [- `xpile_wgsl_codegen::wgpu_adapter_available`]: absence is a clean skip (free CI has no WABT), presence runs the witness (local box).

# xpile_wasm_frontend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/xpile-wasm-frontend/0.1.615/target-redirect/xpile_wasm_frontend/

## Expand description

WebAssembly text (WAT) frontend — the LIFT half of first-class
bidirectional native WASM (PMAT-954, the inverse of the
`Target::Wasm` emit half PMAT-951).

Lifts the **WAT scalar/control subset** — specifically the image of
[`xpile-wasm-codegen`] — back to canonical meta-HIR via a
stack→expression-tree reconstruction with **structured control-flow
recovery** (PMAT-959, the control half of PMAT-952). This is a **lossy
decompilation**, the honest other side of the asymmetry recorded in
`project-bidirectional-wasm`: emit is clean, lift is lossy.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-the-lift-recovers)What the lift recovers

-
The `(module …)`skeleton + its`;; source module: <name>`comment.
-
Each user `(func $name (param …) (result …) (local …) <body>)`: the signature (params →`Param``Type``(local …)`declarations, and a**straight-line**body reconstructed by simulating the WASM operand stack:- `local.get $x`→- `Expr::Ident`- `local.set $x`→ a- `Stmt::Let`- `Stmt::Assign`
- `i64.const`→- `Expr::LitInt`- `f64.const`→- `Expr::LitFloat`- `i32.const`→- `Expr::LitBool`
- `i64.*`/- `f64.*`/- `i32.*`arithmetic & comparison ops → the matching- `BinOp`- `FloatOp`
- `call $__wasm_floordiv_i64`/- `$__wasm_floormod_i64`→ the Python floor- `BinOp::FloorDiv`- `BinOp::Mod`
- `call $f`→ an intra-module- `Expr::Call`
 The single value left on the stack is the `Block::trailing_return`

[§](https://docs.rs#structured-control-flow-recovery-pmat-959)Structured control-flow recovery (PMAT-959)

The lift now inverts the **canonical control shapes** the emit produces,
recursively (the right-inverse-on-image property still holds — it only
needs to invert what `xpile-wasm-codegen` emits, not arbitrary WASM):

- `(block $brk (loop $cont <cond> i32.eqz br_if $brk <body> br $cont))`→- `Stmt::While`- `i32.eqz`+- `br_if $brk`guard is stripped to recover the un-negated loop condition; the trailing- `br $cont`back-edge closes the body.
- `if <then-stmts> [else <else-stmts>] end`(no- `(result …)`) →- `Stmt::If`
- `if (result T) <then-expr> else <else-expr> end`→- `Expr::IfExpr`
- `return`→- `Stmt::Return`
- `br $brk`→- `Stmt::Break`- `br $cont`→- `Stmt::Continue`
- Nested control recurses.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-the-lift-loses--refuses-the-honest-lossy-posture)What the lift loses / refuses (the honest lossy posture)

- **Type identity collapses to the canonical scalar:**- `i64`→- `I64`(a- `CLong`is indistinguishable),- `i32`→- `Bool`(a- `CUInt`/ a raw bool flag are indistinguishable),- `f64`→- `F64`,- `f32`→- `F32`. The high-level Python/Rust type is irreversibly gone.
- **Names**survive only because the emit kept them (- `$x`); a stripped WAT would lose them.
- **Non-canonical control flow**— any block/loop/branch nesting OUTSIDE the- `xpile-wasm-codegen`image (e.g. a- `(block …)`whose label is not- `$brk`, a- `br_table`, a raw stack-machine branch xpile never emits) — is still- **refused**with a hard- `FrontendError::Lower`- `$__wasm_floordiv_i64`/- `$__wasm_floormod_i64`helpers (which DO contain an inner- `(if …)`) are skipped wholesale, not parsed.

[§](https://docs.rs#correctness-witness)Correctness witness

The lift is a **right-inverse of emit on its WAT image** — pinned by
executed round-trip fixed-point tests in `tests.rs`:
`emit(lift(emit(M))) == emit(M)` for every straight-line scalar AND
structured-control fixture (a `while` sum, an `if`/`else` max, an
if-expr, and a nested loop+if). (A full `lift(emit(M)) == M` is *not*
claimed — the type collapse above makes the lift lossy; the fixed point
is the honest, checkable invariant.)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Wasm](https://docs.rs/struct.WasmFrontend.html)- Frontend
- WAT frontend. Lifts the WAT scalar/control subset (the
`xpile-wasm-codegen`image) to meta-HIR.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_wat.html)- wat
- Lift a WAT source string to a meta-HIR `Module``SourceLang::Wasm``Path`).

# xpile_wasm_frontend/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! WebAssembly text (WAT) frontend — the LIFT half of first-class
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//! bidirectional native WASM (PMAT-954, the inverse of the
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! `Target::Wasm` emit half PMAT-951).
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//!

[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! [`xpile-wasm-codegen`] — back to canonical meta-HIR via a
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! stack→expression-tree reconstruction with **structured control-flow
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! recovery** (PMAT-959, the control half of PMAT-952). This is a **lossy
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! decompilation**, the honest other side of the asymmetry recorded in
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! `project-bidirectional-wasm`: emit is clean, lift is lossy.
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//!
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! ## What the lift recovers
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//!
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! - The `(module …)` skeleton + its `;; source module: <name>` comment.
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! - Each user `(func $name (param …) (result …) (local …) <body>)`:
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//!   the signature (params → [`Param`], result → return [`Type`]), the
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//!   `(local …)` declarations, and a **straight-line** body reconstructed
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//!   by simulating the WASM operand stack:
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!     * `local.get $x` → [`Expr::Ident`]; `local.set $x` → a
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//!       [`Stmt::Let`] (first write of a declared local) or
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!       [`Stmt::Assign`].

[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!       `i32.const` → [`Expr::LitBool`] (0/1, the emit's bool encoding).
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//!     * `i64.*` / `f64.*` / `i32.*` arithmetic & comparison ops → the
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!       matching [`BinOp`] / [`FloatOp`].

[27](https://docs.rs#27)//!       Python floor [`BinOp::FloorDiv`] / [`BinOp::Mod`] (the emit's

[30](https://docs.rs#30)//!       callee's parsed signature).

[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! needs to invert what `xpile-wasm-codegen` emits, not arbitrary WASM):

[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!     [`Stmt::If`] (the decy-style statement-if shape).

[48](https://docs.rs#48)//!   * `br $brk` → [`Stmt::Break`]; `br $cont` → [`Stmt::Continue`].
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//!   * Nested control recurses.
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//!

[77](https://docs.rs#77)use std::collections::HashMap;
[78](https://docs.rs#78)use std::path::Path;
[79](https://docs.rs#79)
[80](https://docs.rs#80)use xpile_frontend::{Frontend, FrontendError};
[81](https://docs.rs#81)use xpile_meta_hir::{
[82](https://docs.rs#82)    BinOp, Block, Expr, FloatOp, Function, Item, Module, Param, SourceLang, Stmt, Type,

[85](https://docs.rs#85)/// WAT frontend. Lifts the WAT scalar/control subset (the
[86](https://docs.rs#86)/// `xpile-wasm-codegen` image) to meta-HIR.
[87](https://docs.rs#87)#[derive(Default)]
[88](https://docs.rs#88)pub struct WasmFrontend;
[89](https://docs.rs#89)
[90](https://docs.rs#90)impl WasmFrontend {
[91](https://docs.rs#91)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[92](https://docs.rs#92)        Self
[93](https://docs.rs#93)    }
[94](https://docs.rs#94)}
[95](https://docs.rs#95)
[96](https://docs.rs#96)impl Frontend for WasmFrontend {
[97](https://docs.rs#97)    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
[98](https://docs.rs#98)        "wasm"
[99](https://docs.rs#99)    }
[100](https://docs.rs#100)
[101](https://docs.rs#101)    fn extensions(&self) -> &[&'static str] {
[102](https://docs.rs#102)        &["wat"]
[103](https://docs.rs#103)    }
[104](https://docs.rs#104)
[105](https://docs.rs#105)    fn parse_and_lower(&self, path: &Path, source: &str) -> Result<Module, FrontendError> {
[106](https://docs.rs#106)        let fallback = path
[107](https://docs.rs#107)            .file_stem()
[108](https://docs.rs#108)            .and_then(|s| s.to_str())
[109](https://docs.rs#109)            .unwrap_or("wasm_module");
[110](https://docs.rs#110)        let name = recover_module_name(source, fallback);
[111](https://docs.rs#111)        lift_wat(&name, source)
[112](https://docs.rs#112)    }
[113](https://docs.rs#113)}
[114](https://docs.rs#114)
[115](https://docs.rs#115)/// Lift a WAT source string to a meta-HIR [`Module`] tagged
[116](https://docs.rs#116)/// [`SourceLang::Wasm`]. Exposed for the round-trip witness (which has no
[117](https://docs.rs#117)/// `Path`).
[118](https://docs.rs#118)pub fn lift_wat(module_name: &str, source: &str) -> Result<Module, FrontendError> {
[119](https://docs.rs#119)    let toks = tokenize(source);
[120](https://docs.rs#120)    let mut i = 0usize;
[121](https://docs.rs#121)    expect(&toks, &mut i, "(")?;
[122](https://docs.rs#122)    expect(&toks, &mut i, "module")?;
[123](https://docs.rs#123)
[124](https://docs.rs#124)    // Split the module body into top-level `(func …)` slices (skipping
[125](https://docs.rs#125)    // `(export …)` directives and refusing anything else).
[126](https://docs.rs#126)    let mut func_spans: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new(); // inclusive [open, close]
[127](https://docs.rs#127)    loop {
[128](https://docs.rs#128)        let t = peek(&toks, i)?;
[129](https://docs.rs#129)        if t == ")" {
[130](https://docs.rs#130)            break; // module close
[131](https://docs.rs#131)        }
[132](https://docs.rs#132)        if t != "(" {
[133](https://docs.rs#133)            return Err(FrontendError::Parse(format!(
[134](https://docs.rs#134)                "expected `(` or `)` in module body, found `{t}`"
[135](https://docs.rs#135)            )));
[136](https://docs.rs#136)        }
[137](https://docs.rs#137)        let close = matching_paren(&toks, i)?;
[138](https://docs.rs#138)        let kw = peek(&toks, i + 1)?;
[139](https://docs.rs#139)        match kw.as_str() {
[140](https://docs.rs#140)            "func" => func_spans.push((i, close)),
[141](https://docs.rs#141)            "export" => { /* re-derived from the function on re-emit; skip */ }
[142](https://docs.rs#142)            other => {
[143](https://docs.rs#143)                return Err(FrontendError::Lower(format!(
[144](https://docs.rs#144)                    "WAT top-level `({other} …)` is outside the lift subset \
[145](https://docs.rs#145)                     (only `(func …)` / `(export …)`; memory/import/table/global \
[146](https://docs.rs#146)                     decompilation is deferred to PMAT-952)"
[147](https://docs.rs#147)                )));
[148](https://docs.rs#148)            }
[149](https://docs.rs#149)        }
[150](https://docs.rs#150)        i = close + 1;
[151](https://docs.rs#151)    }
[152](https://docs.rs#152)
[153](https://docs.rs#153)    // Pass 1: arity map (name → param count) over EVERY func, so a
[154](https://docs.rs#154)    // `call $f` knows how many operands to pop — including forward
[155](https://docs.rs#155)    // references and the synthetic helpers.
[156](https://docs.rs#156)    let mut arity: HashMap<String, usize> = HashMap::new();
[157](https://docs.rs#157)    for &(open, close) in &func_spans {
[158](https://docs.rs#158)        let (name, n_params) = parse_func_arity(&toks[open..=close])?;
[159](https://docs.rs#159)        arity.insert(name, n_params);
[160](https://docs.rs#160)    }
[161](https://docs.rs#161)
[162](https://docs.rs#162)    // Pass 2: lift each USER func (skip the synthetic `$__wasm_*` helpers,
[163](https://docs.rs#163)    // whose bodies carry control flow we intentionally do not parse).
[164](https://docs.rs#164)    let mut items = Vec::new();
[165](https://docs.rs#165)    for &(open, close) in &func_spans {
[166](https://docs.rs#166)        let slice = &toks[open..=close];
[167](https://docs.rs#167)        let raw_name = func_name(slice)?;
[168](https://docs.rs#168)        if raw_name.starts_with("__wasm_") {
[169](https://docs.rs#169)            continue;
[170](https://docs.rs#170)        }
[171](https://docs.rs#171)        items.push(Item::Function(lift_function(slice, &arity)?));
[172](https://docs.rs#172)    }
[173](https://docs.rs#173)
[174](https://docs.rs#174)    Ok(Module {
[175](https://docs.rs#175)        name: module_name.to_string(),
[176](https://docs.rs#176)        source_lang: SourceLang::Wasm,
[177](https://docs.rs#177)        items,
[178](https://docs.rs#178)        ffi_boundaries: Vec::new(),
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    })
[180](https://docs.rs#180)}
[181](https://docs.rs#181)
[182](https://docs.rs#182)// ─── Module-name recovery ───────────────────────────────────────────
[183](https://docs.rs#183)
[184](https://docs.rs#184)/// Recover the original module name from the emit's
[185](https://docs.rs#185)/// `;; source module: <name>` comment (which `tokenize` strips), so the
[186](https://docs.rs#186)/// lifted module re-emits an identical header. Falls back to the file
[187](https://docs.rs#187)/// stem when absent.
[188](https://docs.rs#188)fn recover_module_name(src: &str, fallback: &str) -> String {
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    for line in src.lines() {
[190](https://docs.rs#190)        if let Some(rest) = line.trim_start().strip_prefix(";; source module:") {
[191](https://docs.rs#191)            let n = rest.trim();
[192](https://docs.rs#192)            if !n.is_empty() {
[193](https://docs.rs#193)                return n.to_string();
[194](https://docs.rs#194)            }
[195](https://docs.rs#195)        }
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    }
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    fallback.to_string()
[198](https://docs.rs#198)}
[199](https://docs.rs#199)
[200](https://docs.rs#200)// ─── Tokenizer ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[201](https://docs.rs#201)
[202](https://docs.rs#202)/// Tokenize WAT into atoms, with `(` / `)` as standalone tokens and
[203](https://docs.rs#203)/// `;; …`-to-EOL line comments stripped. xpile's emit is one instruction
[204](https://docs.rs#204)/// per line with whitespace-delimited atoms, so this flat tokenizer is
[205](https://docs.rs#205)/// sufficient for the lift subset (float atoms like `2.0` / `-inf` /
[206](https://docs.rs#206)/// `1e30` stay single tokens).
[207](https://docs.rs#207)fn tokenize(src: &str) -> Vec<String> {
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    let mut toks = Vec::new();
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    let mut cur = String::new();
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    let mut chars = src.chars().peekable();
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
[212](https://docs.rs#212)        match c {
[213](https://docs.rs#213)            // `;;` line comment → skip to end of line.
[214](https://docs.rs#214)            ';' if chars.peek() == Some(&';') => {
[215](https://docs.rs#215)                for n in chars.by_ref() {
[216](https://docs.rs#216)                    if n == '\n' {
[217](https://docs.rs#217)                        break;
[218](https://docs.rs#218)                    }
[219](https://docs.rs#219)                }
[220](https://docs.rs#220)            }
[221](https://docs.rs#221)            '(' | ')' => {
[222](https://docs.rs#222)                if !cur.is_empty() {
[223](https://docs.rs#223)                    toks.push(std::mem::take(&mut cur));
[224](https://docs.rs#224)                }
[225](https://docs.rs#225)                toks.push(c.to_string());
[226](https://docs.rs#226)            }
[227](https://docs.rs#227)            c if c.is_whitespace() => {
[228](https://docs.rs#228)                if !cur.is_empty() {
[229](https://docs.rs#229)                    toks.push(std::mem::take(&mut cur));
[230](https://docs.rs#230)                }
[231](https://docs.rs#231)            }
[232](https://docs.rs#232)            c => cur.push(c),
[233](https://docs.rs#233)        }
[234](https://docs.rs#234)    }
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    if !cur.is_empty() {
[236](https://docs.rs#236)        toks.push(cur);
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    }
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    toks
[239](https://docs.rs#239)}
[240](https://docs.rs#240)
[241](https://docs.rs#241)// ─── Token cursor helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────
[242](https://docs.rs#242)
[243](https://docs.rs#243)fn peek(toks: &[String], i: usize) -> Result<&String, FrontendError> {
[244](https://docs.rs#244)    toks.get(i)
[245](https://docs.rs#245)        .ok_or_else(|| FrontendError::Parse("unexpected end of WAT input".to_string()))
[246](https://docs.rs#246)}
[247](https://docs.rs#247)
[248](https://docs.rs#248)fn expect(toks: &[String], i: &mut usize, want: &str) -> Result<(), FrontendError> {
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    let got = peek(toks, *i)?;
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    if got != want {
[251](https://docs.rs#251)        return Err(FrontendError::Parse(format!(
[252](https://docs.rs#252)            "expected `{want}`, found `{got}`"
[253](https://docs.rs#253)        )));
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    }
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    *i += 1;
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    Ok(())
[257](https://docs.rs#257)}
[258](https://docs.rs#258)
[259](https://docs.rs#259)/// Index of the `)` matching the `(` at `open`.
[260](https://docs.rs#260)fn matching_paren(toks: &[String], open: usize) -> Result<usize, FrontendError> {
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    let mut depth = 0usize;
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    for (k, t) in toks.iter().enumerate().skip(open) {
[263](https://docs.rs#263)        match t.as_str() {
[264](https://docs.rs#264)            "(" => depth += 1,
[265](https://docs.rs#265)            ")" => {
[266](https://docs.rs#266)                depth -= 1;
[267](https://docs.rs#267)                if depth == 0 {
[268](https://docs.rs#268)                    return Ok(k);
[269](https://docs.rs#269)                }
[270](https://docs.rs#270)            }
[271](https://docs.rs#271)            _ => {}
[272](https://docs.rs#272)        }
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    }
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    Err(FrontendError::Parse(
[275](https://docs.rs#275)        "unbalanced parentheses in WAT".to_string(),
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    ))
[277](https://docs.rs#277)}
[278](https://docs.rs#278)
[279](https://docs.rs#279)/// Strip a leading `$` from a WAT identifier (meta-HIR names have none).
[280](https://docs.rs#280)fn ident(tok: &str) -> &str {
[281](https://docs.rs#281)    tok.strip_prefix('$').unwrap_or(tok)
[282](https://docs.rs#282)}
[283](https://docs.rs#283)
[284](https://docs.rs#284)// ─── Function header parsing ────────────────────────────────────────
[285](https://docs.rs#285)
[286](https://docs.rs#286)/// The raw (`$`-stripped) name of a `(func $name …)` slice.
[287](https://docs.rs#287)fn func_name(slice: &[String]) -> Result<String, FrontendError> {
[288](https://docs.rs#288)    // slice = [ "(", "func", "$name", … , ")" ]
[289](https://docs.rs#289)    let n = slice
[290](https://docs.rs#290)        .get(2)
[291](https://docs.rs#291)        .ok_or_else(|| FrontendError::Parse("`(func` missing a name".to_string()))?;
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    Ok(ident(n).to_string())
[293](https://docs.rs#293)}
[294](https://docs.rs#294)
[295](https://docs.rs#295)/// Parse just the name + parameter count of a func slice (Pass 1).
[296](https://docs.rs#296)fn parse_func_arity(slice: &[String]) -> Result<(String, usize), FrontendError> {
[297](https://docs.rs#297)    let name = func_name(slice)?;
[298](https://docs.rs#298)    let mut n = 0usize;
[299](https://docs.rs#299)    let mut k = 3; // after "(", "func", "$name"
[300](https://docs.rs#300)    let end = slice.len() - 1; // final ")"
[301](https://docs.rs#301)    while k < end {
[302](https://docs.rs#302)        if slice[k] == "(" && slice.get(k + 1).map(String::as_str) == Some("param") {
[303](https://docs.rs#303)            n += 1;
[304](https://docs.rs#304)            k = local_matching(slice, k)? + 1;
[305](https://docs.rs#305)        } else if slice[k] == "(" {
[306](https://docs.rs#306)            // result / local / control sub-expr — not a param; skip it.
[307](https://docs.rs#307)            k = local_matching(slice, k)? + 1;
[308](https://docs.rs#308)        } else {
[309](https://docs.rs#309)            // First body instruction — params are all before the body.
[310](https://docs.rs#310)            break;
[311](https://docs.rs#311)        }
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    }
[313](https://docs.rs#313)    Ok((name, n))
[314](https://docs.rs#314)}
[315](https://docs.rs#315)
[316](https://docs.rs#316)/// `matching_paren` relative to a slice.
[317](https://docs.rs#317)fn local_matching(slice: &[String], open: usize) -> Result<usize, FrontendError> {
[318](https://docs.rs#318)    matching_paren(slice, open)
[319](https://docs.rs#319)}
[320](https://docs.rs#320)
[321](https://docs.rs#321)/// Map a WAT value type keyword to its canonical meta-HIR [`Type`]. This
[322](https://docs.rs#322)/// is the lossy direction: the emit collapses several meta types onto
[323](https://docs.rs#323)/// each WAT type, so the lift picks the canonical representative.
[324](https://docs.rs#324)fn map_wat_type(kw: &str) -> Result<Type, FrontendError> {
[325](https://docs.rs#325)    match kw {
[326](https://docs.rs#326)        "i64" => Ok(Type::I64),
[327](https://docs.rs#327)        // The emit lowers BOTH `Bool` and `CUInt` to i32; `Bool` is the
[328](https://docs.rs#328)        // canonical representative (the dominant i32 source — comparisons,
[329](https://docs.rs#329)        // bool literals). Re-emits as i32 either way, so the fixed point
[330](https://docs.rs#330)        // holds.
[331](https://docs.rs#331)        "i32" => Ok(Type::Bool),
[332](https://docs.rs#332)        "f64" => Ok(Type::F64),
[333](https://docs.rs#333)        "f32" => Ok(Type::F32),
[334](https://docs.rs#334)        other => Err(FrontendError::Lower(format!(
[335](https://docs.rs#335)            "WAT value type `{other}` is outside the lift subset \
[336](https://docs.rs#336)             (only i64/i32/f64/f32)"
[337](https://docs.rs#337)        ))),
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    }
[339](https://docs.rs#339)}
[340](https://docs.rs#340)
[341](https://docs.rs#341)/// Fully lift one user `(func …)` slice to a meta-HIR [`Function`].
[342](https://docs.rs#342)fn lift_function(
[343](https://docs.rs#343)    slice: &[String],
[344](https://docs.rs#344)    arity: &HashMap<String, usize>,
[345](https://docs.rs#345)) -> Result<Function, FrontendError> {
[346](https://docs.rs#346)    let name = func_name(slice)?;
[347](https://docs.rs#347)    let end = slice.len() - 1; // final ")"
[348](https://docs.rs#348)    let mut k = 3; // after "(", "func", "$name"
[349](https://docs.rs#349)
[350](https://docs.rs#350)    let mut params: Vec<Param> = Vec::new();
[351](https://docs.rs#351)    let mut return_type = Type::Unit;
[352](https://docs.rs#352)    let mut locals: Vec<(String, Type)> = Vec::new();
[353](https://docs.rs#353)    let mut local_names: std::collections::HashSet<String> = std::collections::HashSet::new();
[354](https://docs.rs#354)
[355](https://docs.rs#355)    // Header: zero+ (param …), optional (result …), zero+ (local …).
[356](https://docs.rs#356)    while k < end {
[357](https://docs.rs#357)        if slice[k] != "(" {
[358](https://docs.rs#358)            break; // body begins
[359](https://docs.rs#359)        }
[360](https://docs.rs#360)        let close = local_matching(slice, k)?;
[361](https://docs.rs#361)        let kw = slice
[362](https://docs.rs#362)            .get(k + 1)
[363](https://docs.rs#363)            .ok_or_else(|| FrontendError::Parse("empty `(` form in func header".to_string()))?;
[364](https://docs.rs#364)        match kw.as_str() {
[365](https://docs.rs#365)            "param" => {
[366](https://docs.rs#366)                // ( param $name ty )
[367](https://docs.rs#367)                let pname = ident(peek_slice(slice, k + 2)?);
[368](https://docs.rs#368)                let ty = map_wat_type(peek_slice(slice, k + 3)?)?;
[369](https://docs.rs#369)                params.push(Param {
[370](https://docs.rs#370)                    name: pname.to_string(),
[371](https://docs.rs#371)                    ty,
[372](https://docs.rs#372)                    mutable: false,
[373](https://docs.rs#373)                });
[374](https://docs.rs#374)            }
[375](https://docs.rs#375)            "result" => {
[376](https://docs.rs#376)                // ( result ty )
[377](https://docs.rs#377)                return_type = map_wat_type(peek_slice(slice, k + 2)?)?;
[378](https://docs.rs#378)            }
[379](https://docs.rs#379)            "local" => {
[380](https://docs.rs#380)                // ( local $name ty )
[381](https://docs.rs#381)                let lname = ident(peek_slice(slice, k + 2)?).to_string();
[382](https://docs.rs#382)                let ty = map_wat_type(peek_slice(slice, k + 3)?)?;
[383](https://docs.rs#383)                local_names.insert(lname.clone());
[384](https://docs.rs#384)                locals.push((lname, ty));
[385](https://docs.rs#385)            }
[386](https://docs.rs#386)            // Anything else is the first BODY construct (e.g. a `while`
[387](https://docs.rs#387)            // loop emitted as `(block $brk (loop $cont …))` as the very
[388](https://docs.rs#388)            // first statement) — the header is over, stop and let the
[389](https://docs.rs#389)            // structured body lifter take it (PMAT-959).
[390](https://docs.rs#390)            _ => break,
[391](https://docs.rs#391)        }
[392](https://docs.rs#392)        k = close + 1;
[393](https://docs.rs#393)    }
[394](https://docs.rs#394)
[395](https://docs.rs#395)    // Body: an instruction stream [k, end), now WITH structured control
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    // flow (PMAT-959). Reconstruct via a recursive lifter that simulates
[397](https://docs.rs#397)    // the operand stack AND recovers the canonical control shapes the emit
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    // produces (`(block $brk (loop $cont …))` → `While`, bare
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    // `if … else … end` → `Stmt::If`, `if (result T) …` → `Expr::IfExpr`,
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    // `return` → `Stmt::Return`, `br $brk`/`br $cont` → `Break`/`Continue`).
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    let body_toks = &slice[k..end];
[402](https://docs.rs#402)    let set_counts = count_local_sets(body_toks);
[403](https://docs.rs#403)    let local_ty: HashMap<String, Type> =
[404](https://docs.rs#404)        locals.iter().map(|(n, t)| (n.clone(), t.clone())).collect();
[405](https://docs.rs#405)
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    let mut ctx = BodyCtx {
[407](https://docs.rs#407)        arity,
[408](https://docs.rs#408)        local_names: &local_names,
[409](https://docs.rs#409)        local_ty: &local_ty,
[410](https://docs.rs#410)        set_counts: &set_counts,
[411](https://docs.rs#411)        assigned: std::collections::HashSet::new(),
[412](https://docs.rs#412)    };
[413](https://docs.rs#413)
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    // Lift the whole function body as a top-level block (terminated by the
[415](https://docs.rs#415)    // end of the slice). Any residual operand-stack values are the trailing
[416](https://docs.rs#416)    // return; any structural mismatch is a hard refusal (never a wrong lift).
[417](https://docs.rs#417)    let (stmts, mut stack) = lift_block(body_toks, &mut ctx, BlockEnd::Eof)?;
[418](https://docs.rs#418)
[419](https://docs.rs#419)    // The single residual value is the trailing return (or unit/void).
[420](https://docs.rs#420)    let trailing_return = if matches!(return_type, Type::Unit) {
[421](https://docs.rs#421)        if !stack.is_empty() {
[422](https://docs.rs#422)            return Err(FrontendError::Lower(format!(
[423](https://docs.rs#423)                "void function `{name}` left {} value(s) on the stack",
[424](https://docs.rs#424)                stack.len()
[425](https://docs.rs#425)            )));
[426](https://docs.rs#426)        }
[427](https://docs.rs#427)        Expr::Unit
[428](https://docs.rs#428)    } else {
[429](https://docs.rs#429)        if stack.len() != 1 {
[430](https://docs.rs#430)            return Err(FrontendError::Lower(format!(
[431](https://docs.rs#431)                "function `{name}` did not reconstruct to a single trailing value \
[432](https://docs.rs#432)                 (stack depth {}) — likely outside the straight-line scalar subset",
[433](https://docs.rs#433)                stack.len()
[434](https://docs.rs#434)            )));
[435](https://docs.rs#435)        }
[436](https://docs.rs#436)        stack.pop().unwrap()
[437](https://docs.rs#437)    };
[438](https://docs.rs#438)
[439](https://docs.rs#439)    Ok(Function {
[440](https://docs.rs#440)        name,
[441](https://docs.rs#441)        params,
[442](https://docs.rs#442)        return_type,
[443](https://docs.rs#443)        body: Block {
[444](https://docs.rs#444)            stmts,
[445](https://docs.rs#445)            trailing_return,
[446](https://docs.rs#446)        },
[447](https://docs.rs#447)    })
[448](https://docs.rs#448)}
[449](https://docs.rs#449)
[450](https://docs.rs#450)// ─── Structured body lifter (PMAT-959) ──────────────────────────────
[451](https://docs.rs#451)//
[452](https://docs.rs#452)// A recursive descent over the WAT body token stream that simulates the
[453](https://docs.rs#453)// operand stack AND recovers the canonical control shapes the emit
[454](https://docs.rs#454)// produces. It is a *right-inverse on the emit image*: it inverts exactly
[455](https://docs.rs#455)// what `xpile-wasm-codegen` emits, refusing anything else.
[456](https://docs.rs#456)
[457](https://docs.rs#457)/// Shared lowering context threaded through the recursive body lifter.
[458](https://docs.rs#458)struct BodyCtx<'a> {
[459](https://docs.rs#459)    /// name → param count, for `call $f` arity.
[460](https://docs.rs#460)    arity: &'a HashMap<String, usize>,
[461](https://docs.rs#461)    /// Declared `(local …)` names (drives Let-vs-Assign).
[462](https://docs.rs#462)    local_names: &'a std::collections::HashSet<String>,
[463](https://docs.rs#463)    /// local name → its lifted [`Type`] (for the `Let`'s annotation).
[464](https://docs.rs#464)    local_ty: &'a HashMap<String, Type>,
[465](https://docs.rs#465)    /// `local.set` count per name over the WHOLE body (drives `let mut`).
[466](https://docs.rs#466)    set_counts: &'a HashMap<String, usize>,
[467](https://docs.rs#467)    /// Names already bound by a `Let` (a later set is an `Assign`).
[468](https://docs.rs#468)    assigned: std::collections::HashSet<String>,
[469](https://docs.rs#469)}
[470](https://docs.rs#470)
[471](https://docs.rs#471)/// What terminates the block currently being lifted.
[472](https://docs.rs#472)#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
[473](https://docs.rs#473)enum BlockEnd {
[474](https://docs.rs#474)    /// End of the function body slice (the top-level block).
[475](https://docs.rs#475)    Eof,
[476](https://docs.rs#476)    /// An `else` or `end` keyword (an `if`/`else` arm).
[477](https://docs.rs#477)    ElseOrEnd,
[478](https://docs.rs#478)    /// The matching `)` of a `(loop …)` form (a `while` body).
[479](https://docs.rs#479)    Loop,
[480](https://docs.rs#480)}
[481](https://docs.rs#481)
[482](https://docs.rs#482)/// Outcome of consuming one block: its statements and the residual operand
[483](https://docs.rs#483)/// stack, plus the terminator keyword actually seen (so an `if` lifter can
[484](https://docs.rs#484)/// tell `else` from `end`).
[485](https://docs.rs#485)struct BlockOut {
[486](https://docs.rs#486)    stmts: Vec<Stmt>,
[487](https://docs.rs#487)    stack: Vec<Expr>,
[488](https://docs.rs#488)    /// The terminator token (`"else"`, `"end"`, or `""` for EOF/loop-close).
[489](https://docs.rs#489)    term: String,
[490](https://docs.rs#490)}
[491](https://docs.rs#491)
[492](https://docs.rs#492)/// Lift a block of body tokens, returning its statements and residual stack.
[493](https://docs.rs#493)/// (Convenience wrapper used at the function-body top level.)
[494](https://docs.rs#494)fn lift_block(
[495](https://docs.rs#495)    toks: &[String],
[496](https://docs.rs#496)    ctx: &mut BodyCtx<'_>,
[497](https://docs.rs#497)    end: BlockEnd,
[498](https://docs.rs#498)) -> Result<(Vec<Stmt>, Vec<Expr>), FrontendError> {
[499](https://docs.rs#499)    let out = lift_block_inner(toks, &mut 0usize, ctx, end)?;
[500](https://docs.rs#500)    Ok((out.stmts, out.stack))
[501](https://docs.rs#501)}
[502](https://docs.rs#502)
[503](https://docs.rs#503)/// The core recursive lifter. Consumes tokens from `*pos` until the block
[504](https://docs.rs#504)/// terminator for `end` is reached, simulating the operand stack and
[505](https://docs.rs#505)/// emitting statements for the control shapes / `local.set` / `return`.
[506](https://docs.rs#506)fn lift_block_inner(
[507](https://docs.rs#507)    toks: &[String],
[508](https://docs.rs#508)    pos: &mut usize,
[509](https://docs.rs#509)    ctx: &mut BodyCtx<'_>,
[510](https://docs.rs#510)    end: BlockEnd,
[511](https://docs.rs#511)) -> Result<BlockOut, FrontendError> {
[512](https://docs.rs#512)    let mut stack: Vec<Expr> = Vec::new();
[513](https://docs.rs#513)    let mut stmts: Vec<Stmt> = Vec::new();
[514](https://docs.rs#514)
[515](https://docs.rs#515)    while *pos < toks.len() {
[516](https://docs.rs#516)        let instr = toks[*pos].as_str();
[517](https://docs.rs#517)        match instr {
[518](https://docs.rs#518)            // ── block terminators ──
[519](https://docs.rs#519)            "else" | "end" if end == BlockEnd::ElseOrEnd => {
[520](https://docs.rs#520)                let term = instr.to_string();
[521](https://docs.rs#521)                *pos += 1;
[522](https://docs.rs#522)                return Ok(BlockOut { stmts, stack, term });
[523](https://docs.rs#523)            }
[524](https://docs.rs#524)            // A `(loop …)` body terminates at the loop form's closing `)`.
[525](https://docs.rs#525)            ")" if end == BlockEnd::Loop => {
[526](https://docs.rs#526)                *pos += 1;
[527](https://docs.rs#527)                return Ok(BlockOut {
[528](https://docs.rs#528)                    stmts,
[529](https://docs.rs#529)                    stack,
[530](https://docs.rs#530)                    term: String::new(),
[531](https://docs.rs#531)                });
[532](https://docs.rs#532)            }
[533](https://docs.rs#533)            // ── operand-producing leaves ──
[534](https://docs.rs#534)            "local.get" => {
[535](https://docs.rs#535)                let n = ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?);
[536](https://docs.rs#536)                stack.push(Expr::Ident(n.to_string()));
[537](https://docs.rs#537)                *pos += 2;
[538](https://docs.rs#538)            }
[539](https://docs.rs#539)            "local.set" => {
[540](https://docs.rs#540)                let n = ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?).to_string();
[541](https://docs.rs#541)                let value = pop(&mut stack, instr)?;
[542](https://docs.rs#542)                stmts.push(lift_local_set(n, value, ctx)?);
[543](https://docs.rs#543)                *pos += 2;
[544](https://docs.rs#544)            }
[545](https://docs.rs#545)            "i64.const" => {
[546](https://docs.rs#546)                let v: i64 = peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?
[547](https://docs.rs#547)                    .parse()
[548](https://docs.rs#548)                    .map_err(|_| FrontendError::Parse("bad i64.const literal".to_string()))?;
[549](https://docs.rs#549)                stack.push(Expr::LitInt(v));
[550](https://docs.rs#550)                *pos += 2;
[551](https://docs.rs#551)            }
[552](https://docs.rs#552)            "i32.const" => {
[553](https://docs.rs#553)                let v: i64 = peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?
[554](https://docs.rs#554)                    .parse()
[555](https://docs.rs#555)                    .map_err(|_| FrontendError::Parse("bad i32.const literal".to_string()))?;
[556](https://docs.rs#556)                // In the emit image an i32.const is the 0/1 bool encoding.
[557](https://docs.rs#557)                stack.push(Expr::LitBool(v != 0));
[558](https://docs.rs#558)                *pos += 2;
[559](https://docs.rs#559)            }
[560](https://docs.rs#560)            "f64.const" => {
[561](https://docs.rs#561)                let tok = peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?;
[562](https://docs.rs#562)                let v: f64 = tok
[563](https://docs.rs#563)                    .parse()
[564](https://docs.rs#564)                    .map_err(|_| FrontendError::Parse(format!("bad f64.const literal `{tok}`")))?;
[565](https://docs.rs#565)                stack.push(Expr::LitFloat(v));
[566](https://docs.rs#566)                *pos += 2;
[567](https://docs.rs#567)            }
[568](https://docs.rs#568)            "call" => {
[569](https://docs.rs#569)                let callee = ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?).to_string();
[570](https://docs.rs#570)                lift_call(callee, &mut stack, ctx)?;
[571](https://docs.rs#571)                *pos += 2;
[572](https://docs.rs#572)            }
[573](https://docs.rs#573)            // ── structured control (the PMAT-959 recovery) ──
[574](https://docs.rs#574)            "return" => {
[575](https://docs.rs#575)                // The single residual value (if the fn is non-void) is the
[576](https://docs.rs#576)                // returned expression; a void return takes nothing.
[577](https://docs.rs#577)                let value = if stack.is_empty() {
[578](https://docs.rs#578)                    Expr::Unit
[579](https://docs.rs#579)                } else {
[580](https://docs.rs#580)                    pop(&mut stack, instr)?
[581](https://docs.rs#581)                };
[582](https://docs.rs#582)                stmts.push(Stmt::Return(value));
[583](https://docs.rs#583)                *pos += 1;
[584](https://docs.rs#584)            }
[585](https://docs.rs#585)            "br" => {
[586](https://docs.rs#586)                // `br $brk` → break; `br $cont` → continue (a while body's
[587](https://docs.rs#587)                // back-edge — the trailing `br $cont` is the loop's own and
[588](https://docs.rs#588)                // is consumed by `lift_while`, so any `br` reaching here is a
[589](https://docs.rs#589)                // user break/continue).
[590](https://docs.rs#590)                let label = ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?);
[591](https://docs.rs#591)                match label {
[592](https://docs.rs#592)                    "brk" => stmts.push(Stmt::Break),
[593](https://docs.rs#593)                    "cont" => stmts.push(Stmt::Continue),
[594](https://docs.rs#594)                    other => return Err(refuse_noncanonical(&format!("br ${other}"))),
[595](https://docs.rs#595)                }
[596](https://docs.rs#596)                *pos += 2;
[597](https://docs.rs#597)            }
[598](https://docs.rs#598)            "if" => {
[599](https://docs.rs#599)                lift_if(toks, pos, ctx, &mut stack, &mut stmts)?;
[600](https://docs.rs#600)            }
[601](https://docs.rs#601)            // ── a nested `(…)` form: the `while` idiom, or refuse ──
[602](https://docs.rs#602)            "(" => {
[603](https://docs.rs#603)                let kw = peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?;
[604](https://docs.rs#604)                if kw == "block" {
[605](https://docs.rs#605)                    let while_stmt = lift_while(toks, pos, ctx)?;
[606](https://docs.rs#606)                    stmts.push(while_stmt);
[607](https://docs.rs#607)                } else {
[608](https://docs.rs#608)                    return Err(refuse_noncanonical(kw));
[609](https://docs.rs#609)                }
[610](https://docs.rs#610)            }
[611](https://docs.rs#611)            // ── arithmetic / comparison binary ops ──
[612](https://docs.rs#612)            other => {
[613](https://docs.rs#613)                if let Some(op) = int_binop(other) {
[614](https://docs.rs#614)                    let (lhs, rhs) = pop2(&mut stack, instr)?;
[615](https://docs.rs#615)                    stack.push(Expr::BinOp {
[616](https://docs.rs#616)                        op,
[617](https://docs.rs#617)                        lhs: Box::new(lhs),
[618](https://docs.rs#618)                        rhs: Box::new(rhs),
[619](https://docs.rs#619)                    });
[620](https://docs.rs#620)                    *pos += 1;
[621](https://docs.rs#621)                } else if let Some(fop) = float_binop(other) {
[622](https://docs.rs#622)                    let (lhs, rhs) = pop2(&mut stack, instr)?;
[623](https://docs.rs#623)                    stack.push(Expr::FloatBinOp {
[624](https://docs.rs#624)                        op: fop,
[625](https://docs.rs#625)                        lhs: Box::new(lhs),
[626](https://docs.rs#626)                        rhs: Box::new(rhs),
[627](https://docs.rs#627)                    });
[628](https://docs.rs#628)                    *pos += 1;
[629](https://docs.rs#629)                } else {
[630](https://docs.rs#630)                    return Err(refuse_control(other));
[631](https://docs.rs#631)                }
[632](https://docs.rs#632)            }
[633](https://docs.rs#633)        }
[634](https://docs.rs#634)    }
[635](https://docs.rs#635)
[636](https://docs.rs#636)    // Reached the end of the slice.
[637](https://docs.rs#637)    if end != BlockEnd::Eof {
[638](https://docs.rs#638)        return Err(FrontendError::Parse(
[639](https://docs.rs#639)            "WAT block ended before its `else`/`end`/`)` terminator".to_string(),
[640](https://docs.rs#640)        ));
[641](https://docs.rs#641)    }
[642](https://docs.rs#642)    Ok(BlockOut {
[643](https://docs.rs#643)        stmts,
[644](https://docs.rs#644)        stack,
[645](https://docs.rs#645)        term: String::new(),
[646](https://docs.rs#646)    })
[647](https://docs.rs#647)}
[648](https://docs.rs#648)
[649](https://docs.rs#649)/// Lift a `local.set $n` into a `Let` (first write of a declared local) or
[650](https://docs.rs#650)/// an `Assign` (a re-write / a non-declared name).
[651](https://docs.rs#651)fn lift_local_set(n: String, value: Expr, ctx: &mut BodyCtx<'_>) -> Result<Stmt, FrontendError> {
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    if ctx.local_names.contains(&n) && !ctx.assigned.contains(&n) {
[653](https://docs.rs#653)        let ty = ctx
[654](https://docs.rs#654)            .local_ty
[655](https://docs.rs#655)            .get(&n)
[656](https://docs.rs#656)            .ok_or_else(|| FrontendError::Parse(format!("unknown local `{n}`")))?
[657](https://docs.rs#657)            .clone();
[658](https://docs.rs#658)        let mutable = ctx.set_counts.get(&n).copied().unwrap_or(0) > 1;
[659](https://docs.rs#659)        ctx.assigned.insert(n.clone());
[660](https://docs.rs#660)        Ok(Stmt::Let {
[661](https://docs.rs#661)            name: n,
[662](https://docs.rs#662)            ty,
[663](https://docs.rs#663)            value,
[664](https://docs.rs#664)            mutable,
[665](https://docs.rs#665)        })
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    } else {
[667](https://docs.rs#667)        Ok(Stmt::Assign { name: n, value })
[668](https://docs.rs#668)    }
[669](https://docs.rs#669)}
[670](https://docs.rs#670)
[671](https://docs.rs#671)/// Lift a `call $f` (a helper call → the high-level op, or an intra-module
[672](https://docs.rs#672)/// call → [`Expr::Call`]), pushing the result onto `stack`.
[673](https://docs.rs#673)fn lift_call(
[674](https://docs.rs#674)    callee: String,
[675](https://docs.rs#675)    stack: &mut Vec<Expr>,
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    ctx: &BodyCtx<'_>,
[677](https://docs.rs#677)) -> Result<(), FrontendError> {
[678](https://docs.rs#678)    match callee.as_str() {
[679](https://docs.rs#679)        "__wasm_floordiv_i64" => {
[680](https://docs.rs#680)            let (lhs, rhs) = pop2(stack, "call")?;
[681](https://docs.rs#681)            stack.push(Expr::BinOp {
[682](https://docs.rs#682)                op: BinOp::FloorDiv,
[683](https://docs.rs#683)                lhs: Box::new(lhs),
[684](https://docs.rs#684)                rhs: Box::new(rhs),
[685](https://docs.rs#685)            });
[686](https://docs.rs#686)        }
[687](https://docs.rs#687)        "__wasm_floormod_i64" => {
[688](https://docs.rs#688)            let (lhs, rhs) = pop2(stack, "call")?;
[689](https://docs.rs#689)            stack.push(Expr::BinOp {
[690](https://docs.rs#690)                op: BinOp::Mod,
[691](https://docs.rs#691)                lhs: Box::new(lhs),
[692](https://docs.rs#692)                rhs: Box::new(rhs),
[693](https://docs.rs#693)            });
[694](https://docs.rs#694)        }
[695](https://docs.rs#695)        _ => {
[696](https://docs.rs#696)            let n = *ctx.arity.get(&callee).ok_or_else(|| {
[697](https://docs.rs#697)                FrontendError::Lower(format!(
[698](https://docs.rs#698)                    "call to unknown function `{callee}` (no parsed signature)"
[699](https://docs.rs#699)                ))
[700](https://docs.rs#700)            })?;
[701](https://docs.rs#701)            let mut args = Vec::with_capacity(n);
[702](https://docs.rs#702)            for _ in 0..n {
[703](https://docs.rs#703)                args.push(pop(stack, "call")?);
[704](https://docs.rs#704)            }
[705](https://docs.rs#705)            args.reverse();
[706](https://docs.rs#706)            stack.push(Expr::Call { callee, args });
[707](https://docs.rs#707)        }
[708](https://docs.rs#708)    }
[709](https://docs.rs#709)    Ok(())
[710](https://docs.rs#710)}
[711](https://docs.rs#711)
[712](https://docs.rs#712)/// Lift an `if` form — distinguishing the **if-expression** shape
[713](https://docs.rs#713)/// `if (result T) <then> else <else> end` (pushes an [`Expr::IfExpr`]) from
[714](https://docs.rs#714)/// the **statement-if** shape `if <then-stmts> [else <else-stmts>] end`
[715](https://docs.rs#715)/// (emits a [`Stmt::If`]). The condition is the value already on top of
[716](https://docs.rs#716)/// `stack` (the emit pushes it just before the `if`).
[717](https://docs.rs#717)fn lift_if(
[718](https://docs.rs#718)    toks: &[String],
[719](https://docs.rs#719)    pos: &mut usize,
[720](https://docs.rs#720)    ctx: &mut BodyCtx<'_>,
[721](https://docs.rs#721)    stack: &mut Vec<Expr>,
[722](https://docs.rs#722)    stmts: &mut Vec<Stmt>,
[723](https://docs.rs#723)) -> Result<(), FrontendError> {
[724](https://docs.rs#724)    // The condition is the residual operand.
[725](https://docs.rs#725)    let cond = pop(stack, "if")?;
[726](https://docs.rs#726)    *pos += 1; // consume `if`
[727](https://docs.rs#727)
[728](https://docs.rs#728)    // An if-EXPRESSION is `if (result T) …` — the next tokens are
[729](https://docs.rs#729)    // `( result <ty> )`. Detect and skip that prefix.
[730](https://docs.rs#730)    let is_expr = peek_slice(toks, *pos)? == "(" && peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)? == "result";
[731](https://docs.rs#731)    if is_expr {
[732](https://docs.rs#732)        // skip `( result <ty> )`
[733](https://docs.rs#733)        let close = matching_paren(toks, *pos)?;
[734](https://docs.rs#734)        *pos = close + 1;
[735](https://docs.rs#735)
[736](https://docs.rs#736)        // then-arm: must reduce to exactly one operand.
[737](https://docs.rs#737)        let then_out = lift_block_inner(toks, pos, ctx, BlockEnd::ElseOrEnd)?;
[738](https://docs.rs#738)        if then_out.term != "else" {
[739](https://docs.rs#739)            return Err(refuse_noncanonical(
[740](https://docs.rs#740)                "if (result …) without an `else` arm (xpile always emits both)",
[741](https://docs.rs#741)            ));
[742](https://docs.rs#742)        }
[743](https://docs.rs#743)        let then_expr = single_value(then_out, "if-expr then-arm")?;
[744](https://docs.rs#744)
[745](https://docs.rs#745)        // else-arm: also exactly one operand, terminated by `end`.
[746](https://docs.rs#746)        let else_out = lift_block_inner(toks, pos, ctx, BlockEnd::ElseOrEnd)?;
[747](https://docs.rs#747)        if else_out.term != "end" {
[748](https://docs.rs#748)            return Err(refuse_noncanonical(
[749](https://docs.rs#749)                "if (result …) else-arm not closed by `end`",
[750](https://docs.rs#750)            ));
[751](https://docs.rs#751)        }
[752](https://docs.rs#752)        let else_expr = single_value(else_out, "if-expr else-arm")?;
[753](https://docs.rs#753)
[754](https://docs.rs#754)        stack.push(Expr::IfExpr {
[755](https://docs.rs#755)            cond: Box::new(cond),
[756](https://docs.rs#756)            then_expr: Box::new(then_expr),
[757](https://docs.rs#757)            else_expr: Box::new(else_expr),
[758](https://docs.rs#758)        });
[759](https://docs.rs#759)        return Ok(());
[760](https://docs.rs#760)    }
[761](https://docs.rs#761)
[762](https://docs.rs#762)    // A statement-`if`: arms are statement blocks (no residual value).
[763](https://docs.rs#763)    let then_out = lift_block_inner(toks, pos, ctx, BlockEnd::ElseOrEnd)?;
[764](https://docs.rs#764)    let then_body = stmts_only(then_out.stmts, then_out.stack, "if then-body")?;
[765](https://docs.rs#765)
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    let else_body = match then_out.term.as_str() {
[767](https://docs.rs#767)        "else" => {
[768](https://docs.rs#768)            let else_out = lift_block_inner(toks, pos, ctx, BlockEnd::ElseOrEnd)?;
[769](https://docs.rs#769)            if else_out.term != "end" {
[770](https://docs.rs#770)                return Err(FrontendError::Parse(
[771](https://docs.rs#771)                    "statement-if else-arm not closed by `end`".to_string(),
[772](https://docs.rs#772)                ));
[773](https://docs.rs#773)            }
[774](https://docs.rs#774)            stmts_only(else_out.stmts, else_out.stack, "if else-body")?
[775](https://docs.rs#775)        }
[776](https://docs.rs#776)        "end" => Vec::new(),
[777](https://docs.rs#777)        other => {
[778](https://docs.rs#778)            return Err(FrontendError::Parse(format!(
[779](https://docs.rs#779)                "statement-if then-arm closed by unexpected `{other}`"
[780](https://docs.rs#780)            )))
[781](https://docs.rs#781)        }
[782](https://docs.rs#782)    };
[783](https://docs.rs#783)
[784](https://docs.rs#784)    stmts.push(Stmt::If {
[785](https://docs.rs#785)        cond,
[786](https://docs.rs#786)        then_body,
[787](https://docs.rs#787)        else_body,
[788](https://docs.rs#788)    });
[789](https://docs.rs#789)    Ok(())
[790](https://docs.rs#790)}
[791](https://docs.rs#791)
[792](https://docs.rs#792)/// Lift the canonical `while` idiom:
[793](https://docs.rs#793)/// `(block $brk (loop $cont <cond> i32.eqz br_if $brk <body> br $cont))`.
[794](https://docs.rs#794)/// `*pos` is at the opening `(` of the `(block …)`.
[795](https://docs.rs#795)fn lift_while(
[796](https://docs.rs#796)    toks: &[String],
[797](https://docs.rs#797)    pos: &mut usize,
[798](https://docs.rs#798)    ctx: &mut BodyCtx<'_>,
[799](https://docs.rs#799)) -> Result<Stmt, FrontendError> {
[800](https://docs.rs#800)    // `( block $brk`
[801](https://docs.rs#801)    expect(toks, pos, "(")?;
[802](https://docs.rs#802)    expect(toks, pos, "block")?;
[803](https://docs.rs#803)    if ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos)?) != "brk" {
[804](https://docs.rs#804)        return Err(refuse_noncanonical("(block …) whose label is not $brk"));
[805](https://docs.rs#805)    }
[806](https://docs.rs#806)    *pos += 1; // $brk
[807](https://docs.rs#807)
[808](https://docs.rs#808)    // `( loop $cont`
[809](https://docs.rs#809)    expect(toks, pos, "(")?;
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    expect(toks, pos, "loop")?;
[811](https://docs.rs#811)    if ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos)?) != "cont" {
[812](https://docs.rs#812)        return Err(refuse_noncanonical("(loop …) whose label is not $cont"));
[813](https://docs.rs#813)    }
[814](https://docs.rs#814)    *pos += 1; // $cont
[815](https://docs.rs#815)
[816](https://docs.rs#816)    // <cond instrs> i32.eqz br_if $brk — lift the condition by simulating
[817](https://docs.rs#817)    // the operand stack until the `i32.eqz` guard, which negates the loop
[818](https://docs.rs#818)    // test (the emit's `while c` → `c i32.eqz br_if $brk`).
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    let cond = lift_loop_cond(toks, pos, ctx)?;
[820](https://docs.rs#820)
[821](https://docs.rs#821)    // <body stmts> br $cont — the loop body is a statement block whose
[822](https://docs.rs#822)    // trailing `br $cont` back-edge closes it; then the loop's `)` and the
[823](https://docs.rs#823)    // block's `)`.
[824](https://docs.rs#824)    let body_out = lift_loop_body(toks, pos, ctx)?;
[825](https://docs.rs#825)
[826](https://docs.rs#826)    Ok(Stmt::While {
[827](https://docs.rs#827)        cond,
[828](https://docs.rs#828)        body: body_out,
[829](https://docs.rs#829)    })
[830](https://docs.rs#830)}
[831](https://docs.rs#831)
[832](https://docs.rs#832)/// Lift the loop condition: the operand-stack instructions up to and
[833](https://docs.rs#833)/// including `i32.eqz br_if $brk` (the negated loop test). Returns the
[834](https://docs.rs#834)/// recovered (un-negated) condition expression.
[835](https://docs.rs#835)fn lift_loop_cond(
[836](https://docs.rs#836)    toks: &[String],
[837](https://docs.rs#837)    pos: &mut usize,
[838](https://docs.rs#838)    ctx: &mut BodyCtx<'_>,
[839](https://docs.rs#839)) -> Result<Expr, FrontendError> {
[840](https://docs.rs#840)    let mut stack: Vec<Expr> = Vec::new();
[841](https://docs.rs#841)    loop {
[842](https://docs.rs#842)        let instr = peek_slice(toks, *pos)?;
[843](https://docs.rs#843)        match instr {
[844](https://docs.rs#844)            "i32.eqz" => {
[845](https://docs.rs#845)                // The negation guard. The next two tokens MUST be
[846](https://docs.rs#846)                // `br_if $brk`; the value on the stack is the un-negated
[847](https://docs.rs#847)                // condition.
[848](https://docs.rs#848)                *pos += 1;
[849](https://docs.rs#849)                expect(toks, pos, "br_if")?;
[850](https://docs.rs#850)                if ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos)?) != "brk" {
[851](https://docs.rs#851)                    return Err(refuse_noncanonical("loop guard `br_if` not targeting $brk"));
[852](https://docs.rs#852)                }
[853](https://docs.rs#853)                *pos += 1; // $brk
[854](https://docs.rs#854)                if stack.len() != 1 {
[855](https://docs.rs#855)                    return Err(refuse_noncanonical(
[856](https://docs.rs#856)                        "loop condition did not reduce to a single value",
[857](https://docs.rs#857)                    ));
[858](https://docs.rs#858)                }
[859](https://docs.rs#859)                return Ok(stack.pop().unwrap());
[860](https://docs.rs#860)            }
[861](https://docs.rs#861)            "local.get" => {
[862](https://docs.rs#862)                let n = ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?);
[863](https://docs.rs#863)                stack.push(Expr::Ident(n.to_string()));
[864](https://docs.rs#864)                *pos += 2;
[865](https://docs.rs#865)            }
[866](https://docs.rs#866)            "i64.const" => {
[867](https://docs.rs#867)                let v: i64 = peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?
[868](https://docs.rs#868)                    .parse()
[869](https://docs.rs#869)                    .map_err(|_| FrontendError::Parse("bad i64.const in loop cond".to_string()))?;
[870](https://docs.rs#870)                stack.push(Expr::LitInt(v));
[871](https://docs.rs#871)                *pos += 2;
[872](https://docs.rs#872)            }
[873](https://docs.rs#873)            "i32.const" => {
[874](https://docs.rs#874)                let v: i64 = peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?
[875](https://docs.rs#875)                    .parse()
[876](https://docs.rs#876)                    .map_err(|_| FrontendError::Parse("bad i32.const in loop cond".to_string()))?;
[877](https://docs.rs#877)                stack.push(Expr::LitBool(v != 0));
[878](https://docs.rs#878)                *pos += 2;
[879](https://docs.rs#879)            }
[880](https://docs.rs#880)            "f64.const" => {
[881](https://docs.rs#881)                let tok = peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?;
[882](https://docs.rs#882)                let v: f64 = tok.parse().map_err(|_| {
[883](https://docs.rs#883)                    FrontendError::Parse(format!("bad f64.const `{tok}` in loop cond"))
[884](https://docs.rs#884)                })?;
[885](https://docs.rs#885)                stack.push(Expr::LitFloat(v));
[886](https://docs.rs#886)                *pos += 2;
[887](https://docs.rs#887)            }
[888](https://docs.rs#888)            "call" => {
[889](https://docs.rs#889)                let callee = ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?).to_string();
[890](https://docs.rs#890)                lift_call(callee, &mut stack, ctx)?;
[891](https://docs.rs#891)                *pos += 2;
[892](https://docs.rs#892)            }
[893](https://docs.rs#893)            other => {
[894](https://docs.rs#894)                if let Some(op) = int_binop(other) {
[895](https://docs.rs#895)                    let (lhs, rhs) = pop2(&mut stack, instr)?;
[896](https://docs.rs#896)                    stack.push(Expr::BinOp {
[897](https://docs.rs#897)                        op,
[898](https://docs.rs#898)                        lhs: Box::new(lhs),
[899](https://docs.rs#899)                        rhs: Box::new(rhs),
[900](https://docs.rs#900)                    });
[901](https://docs.rs#901)                    *pos += 1;
[902](https://docs.rs#902)                } else if let Some(fop) = float_binop(other) {
[903](https://docs.rs#903)                    let (lhs, rhs) = pop2(&mut stack, instr)?;
[904](https://docs.rs#904)                    stack.push(Expr::FloatBinOp {
[905](https://docs.rs#905)                        op: fop,
[906](https://docs.rs#906)                        lhs: Box::new(lhs),
[907](https://docs.rs#907)                        rhs: Box::new(rhs),
[908](https://docs.rs#908)                    });
[909](https://docs.rs#909)                    *pos += 1;
[910](https://docs.rs#910)                } else {
[911](https://docs.rs#911)                    return Err(refuse_noncanonical(&format!(
[912](https://docs.rs#912)                        "loop condition contains `{other}` before the `i32.eqz` guard"
[913](https://docs.rs#913)                    )));
[914](https://docs.rs#914)                }
[915](https://docs.rs#915)            }
[916](https://docs.rs#916)        }
[917](https://docs.rs#917)    }
[918](https://docs.rs#918)}
[919](https://docs.rs#919)
[920](https://docs.rs#920)/// Lift the loop body: statements up to the trailing `br $cont` back-edge,
[921](https://docs.rs#921)/// then the loop's `)` and the surrounding block's `)`.
[922](https://docs.rs#922)fn lift_loop_body(
[923](https://docs.rs#923)    toks: &[String],
[924](https://docs.rs#924)    pos: &mut usize,
[925](https://docs.rs#925)    ctx: &mut BodyCtx<'_>,
[926](https://docs.rs#926)) -> Result<Vec<Stmt>, FrontendError> {
[927](https://docs.rs#927)    // The body is a statement block; the emit always ends it with the
[928](https://docs.rs#928)    // `br $cont` back-edge immediately before the loop's `)`. We lift
[929](https://docs.rs#929)    // statements until we hit that trailing `br $cont )`.
[930](https://docs.rs#930)    let mut stmts: Vec<Stmt> = Vec::new();
[931](https://docs.rs#931)    let mut stack: Vec<Expr> = Vec::new();
[932](https://docs.rs#932)    loop {
[933](https://docs.rs#933)        let instr = peek_slice(toks, *pos)?;
[934](https://docs.rs#934)        // The trailing back-edge: `br $cont` followed by the loop close `)`.
[935](https://docs.rs#935)        if instr == "br"
[936](https://docs.rs#936)            && ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?) == "cont"
[937](https://docs.rs#937)            && peek_slice(toks, *pos + 2)? == ")"
[938](https://docs.rs#938)        {
[939](https://docs.rs#939)            *pos += 2; // consume `br $cont`
[940](https://docs.rs#940)            expect(toks, pos, ")")?; // loop close
[941](https://docs.rs#941)            expect(toks, pos, ")")?; // block close
[942](https://docs.rs#942)            if !stack.is_empty() {
[943](https://docs.rs#943)                return Err(refuse_noncanonical(
[944](https://docs.rs#944)                    "while body left a residual value on the operand stack",
[945](https://docs.rs#945)                ));
[946](https://docs.rs#946)            }
[947](https://docs.rs#947)            return Ok(stmts);
[948](https://docs.rs#948)        }
[949](https://docs.rs#949)        // Otherwise lift one body construct via a one-shot sub-block that
[950](https://docs.rs#950)        // stops at the back-edge. Simplest: reuse the leaf/control handling
[951](https://docs.rs#951)        // inline by delegating to lift_block_inner with a sentinel is hard
[952](https://docs.rs#952)        // (no keyword terminator), so we hand-walk here mirroring the leaf
[953](https://docs.rs#953)        // cases, recursing for nested control.
[954](https://docs.rs#954)        match instr {
[955](https://docs.rs#955)            "local.get" => {
[956](https://docs.rs#956)                let n = ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?);
[957](https://docs.rs#957)                stack.push(Expr::Ident(n.to_string()));
[958](https://docs.rs#958)                *pos += 2;
[959](https://docs.rs#959)            }
[960](https://docs.rs#960)            "local.set" => {
[961](https://docs.rs#961)                let n = ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?).to_string();
[962](https://docs.rs#962)                let value = pop(&mut stack, instr)?;
[963](https://docs.rs#963)                stmts.push(lift_local_set(n, value, ctx)?);
[964](https://docs.rs#964)                *pos += 2;
[965](https://docs.rs#965)            }
[966](https://docs.rs#966)            "i64.const" => {
[967](https://docs.rs#967)                let v: i64 = peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?
[968](https://docs.rs#968)                    .parse()
[969](https://docs.rs#969)                    .map_err(|_| FrontendError::Parse("bad i64.const in loop body".to_string()))?;
[970](https://docs.rs#970)                stack.push(Expr::LitInt(v));
[971](https://docs.rs#971)                *pos += 2;
[972](https://docs.rs#972)            }
[973](https://docs.rs#973)            "i32.const" => {
[974](https://docs.rs#974)                let v: i64 = peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?
[975](https://docs.rs#975)                    .parse()
[976](https://docs.rs#976)                    .map_err(|_| FrontendError::Parse("bad i32.const in loop body".to_string()))?;
[977](https://docs.rs#977)                stack.push(Expr::LitBool(v != 0));
[978](https://docs.rs#978)                *pos += 2;
[979](https://docs.rs#979)            }
[980](https://docs.rs#980)            "f64.const" => {
[981](https://docs.rs#981)                let tok = peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?;
[982](https://docs.rs#982)                let v: f64 = tok.parse().map_err(|_| {
[983](https://docs.rs#983)                    FrontendError::Parse(format!("bad f64.const `{tok}` in loop body"))
[984](https://docs.rs#984)                })?;
[985](https://docs.rs#985)                stack.push(Expr::LitFloat(v));
[986](https://docs.rs#986)                *pos += 2;
[987](https://docs.rs#987)            }
[988](https://docs.rs#988)            "call" => {
[989](https://docs.rs#989)                let callee = ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?).to_string();
[990](https://docs.rs#990)                lift_call(callee, &mut stack, ctx)?;
[991](https://docs.rs#991)                *pos += 2;
[992](https://docs.rs#992)            }
[993](https://docs.rs#993)            "return" => {
[994](https://docs.rs#994)                let value = if stack.is_empty() {
[995](https://docs.rs#995)                    Expr::Unit
[996](https://docs.rs#996)                } else {
[997](https://docs.rs#997)                    pop(&mut stack, instr)?
[998](https://docs.rs#998)                };
[999](https://docs.rs#999)                stmts.push(Stmt::Return(value));
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)                *pos += 1;
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)            }
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)            "br" => {
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)                let label = ident(peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?);
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)                match label {
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)                    "brk" => stmts.push(Stmt::Break),
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)                    "cont" => stmts.push(Stmt::Continue),
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)                    other => return Err(refuse_noncanonical(&format!("br ${other}"))),
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)                }
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)                *pos += 2;
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)            }
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)            "if" => {
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)                lift_if(toks, pos, ctx, &mut stack, &mut stmts)?;
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)            }
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)            "(" => {
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)                let kw = peek_slice(toks, *pos + 1)?;
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)                if kw == "block" {
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)                    let while_stmt = lift_while(toks, pos, ctx)?;
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)                    stmts.push(while_stmt);
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)                } else {
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)                    return Err(refuse_noncanonical(kw));
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)                }
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)            }
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)            other => {
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)                if let Some(op) = int_binop(other) {
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)                    let (lhs, rhs) = pop2(&mut stack, instr)?;
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)                    stack.push(Expr::BinOp {
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)                        op,
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)                        lhs: Box::new(lhs),
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)                        rhs: Box::new(rhs),
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)                    });
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)                    *pos += 1;
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)                } else if let Some(fop) = float_binop(other) {
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)                    let (lhs, rhs) = pop2(&mut stack, instr)?;
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)                    stack.push(Expr::FloatBinOp {
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)                        op: fop,
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)                        lhs: Box::new(lhs),
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)                        rhs: Box::new(rhs),
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)                    });
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)                    *pos += 1;
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)                } else {
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)                    return Err(refuse_control(other));
[1042](https://docs.rs#1042)                }
[1043](https://docs.rs#1043)            }
[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)        }
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)    }
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)}

[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)/// Require a block to have reduced to exactly one operand (an if-expr arm).
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)fn single_value(out: BlockOut, what: &str) -> Result<Expr, FrontendError> {
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)    if !out.stmts.is_empty() || out.stack.len() != 1 {
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)        return Err(refuse_noncanonical(&format!(
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)            "{what} did not reduce to a single value (got {} stmt(s), stack depth {})",
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)            out.stmts.len(),
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)            out.stack.len()
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)        )));
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)    }
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)    Ok(out.stack.into_iter().next().unwrap())
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)}
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)/// Require a statement block to have left NO residual operand (a
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)/// statement-if arm).
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)fn stmts_only(stmts: Vec<Stmt>, stack: Vec<Expr>, what: &str) -> Result<Vec<Stmt>, FrontendError> {
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)    if !stack.is_empty() {
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)        return Err(refuse_noncanonical(&format!(
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)            "{what} left {} residual operand(s) on the stack",
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)            stack.len()
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)        )));
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)    }
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)    Ok(stmts)
